grades.quote: On the RISC-V this instruction is amoswap r, a. amoswap reads the value at the memory address a, writes the contents of register r to that address, and puts the value it read into r. That is, it swaps the contents of the register and the addressed memory location. It performs this sequence atomically
grades.reason: It shows how RISC-V implements a lock acquire with an atomic instruction, amoswap. This is the hardware primitive xv6 uses where ARM would use load-exclusive/store-exclusive. It does not mention LR/SC or ARM, so it only partly answers the question about a direct analogue.
It covers re-entrant versus non-re-entrant locks in xv6. It says nothing about the atomic primitive used to implement a lock.
It covers lock granularity and when to use locks. It does not cover the RISC-V atomic instruction used to implement a lock.
